sections.overview: Serripes groenlandicus is a marine bivalve in the cockle family Cardiidae.
sections.identification: It is usually 50–70 mm long, may reach 100 mm, and is grey to brown with a glossy shell.
sections.habitat: It lives on varied seabed sediments, mainly in the sublittoral zone.
sections.diet: It feeds by filtering suspended particles from the water.
sections.behavior: The consulted species records do not describe active movement or other behavior.
sections.reproduction: SeaLifeBase describes free-swimming trochophore larvae followed by veliger larvae; a species-specific spawning season was not found.
sections.ecology: It is a benthic bivalve with a boreal-Arctic distribution, reported from Arctic, northern Atlantic and northern Pacific waters.
sections.conservation: SeaLifeBase reports that the species has not been evaluated by the IUCN.
